items.title: Audible turns to AI to help users discover audiobooks
items.excerpt: Audible's new AI-generated audio previews summarize a book's themes and what readers liked about it, in addition to playing the narrated sample.

items.title: Audible Debuts Audio Discovery and Expands Ask a Question and Recaps
items.excerpt: Audible launches AI 'Audio Discovery' previews and widens its AI Ask a Question and Recaps features to more titles, personalizing finding, going deeper and resuming listening. (Same story as TechCrunch; different angle on Ask/Recaps expansion.)

items.title: How I've Used AI to Improve My Writing Business
items.excerpt: Most discussion of AI in the writing and publishing community has focused on its harms. Jane Friedman details how she has put AI to work in her publishing-industry business.

items.title: Beyond the Download: What Counts as Scholarly Content Use in the Age of AI?
items.excerpt: New usage metrics are needed as AI assistants intermediate between researchers and publisher content. What should count, and what can those numbers say about the value of research?

items.title: The Anatomy of 'Harm': An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
items.excerpt: IFRRO's CEO discusses a study detailing the harm generative AI causes publishers and authors, and what it means for licensing and copyright policy.

items.title: From AI Adoption to AI Practice: Building Governed AI in Scholarly Publishing
items.excerpt: How a publisher can make AI useful across the organization while keeping control of confidential information, editorial decisions and accountability.

items.title: Publishing Ireland conference: AI and rising costs high on the agenda
items.excerpt: Publishing Ireland's annual autumn conference tackled AI, rising costs across the book trade and how Irish regional content can sell. (AI is one of several topics; check body depth.)

items.title: What Would William Blake Have Thought of AI?
items.excerpt: An essay reading William Blake's ideas about images and icons against generative AI. (Opinion/essay; weak news hook.)

items.title: Investigations targeting BIPOC authors
items.excerpt: AI-use accusations rocking French publishing add to a pattern of allegations aimed at BIPOC authors. (Follow-up angle on the French AI scandal covered 11-15.)

items.title: Equity Puts UK-First AI Protections to a Member Vote; voiceover artists get a ballot too
items.excerpt: Almost 8,000 UK film and TV performers, voiceover artists included, can vote until 30 November on a deal with AI likeness protections. (Film/TV pact; books link is narration voices only.)

items.title: 'It's like the wild west': how AI has rocked the literary world
items.excerpt: With authors losing lucrative deals and writers removed from prize shortlists, accusations of AI use are sending shock waves through publishing. Is it too late to turn the tide on machine writing? (Off-list: on-list feeds thin.)

items.title: Author Says the Hundreds of Full-Length Romance Novels She Publishes Every Year Are Very High Quality in Spite of AI Usage
items.excerpt: South African writer Coral Hart insists her AI-generated romance novels, produced by the hundreds each year, are solid because they draw on numerous large language models. (Off-list.)

items.title: New French literary prize will reward work created with AI help
items.excerpt: Three tech-entrepreneurs have created the Pascal Prize to honor a work written with AI help, running counter to most French publishers and authors who oppose machine-hybridized writing. (Off-list; date from Le Monde RSS, page paywalled.)

items.title: Australian Society of Authors, media organisations launch 'Not AI's to Take' campaign
items.excerpt: The Australian Society of Authors and media organisations have launched a 'Not AI's to Take' campaign against AI training on creators' work without consent. (Off-list; body paywalled, date from RSS.)

items.title: Copyright agreements allow use of content for AI prompts
items.excerpt: Australian copyright licensing agreements now permit licensed content to be used in AI prompts. (Off-list; body paywalled, date from RSS.)
